newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU official sees more mkt-oriented farm reform.
newsitem.headline: EU official sees more mkt-oriented farm reform.

text.p: The European Union will continue market-oriented agricultural reforms started in 1992 in order to become more competitive in world markets, said an aide to EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler.
After starting with oilseeds and cereals, the EU is now looking at reform of wine, dairy, olive oil and tobacco markets.
"Further reform is needed independently of the next round of world trade talks and EU enlargement," said John Bensted-Smith, who advises Fischler on market policy.

The immediate priority was to resolve beef market problems linked to the mad cow disease public health scare, he said, adding that EU member states were unlikely to show much enthusiasm for further cereals reform.
But structural changes in other sectors would help the EU prepare for these two major challenges, Bensted-Smith told an Agra Europe Conference on EU farm reform to 2000 and beyond.
"We should not be too pessimistic about our ability to comply (with the world farm trade accord)," he said, noting that it aimed at expanding world trade.
In order to keep within export subsidy limits, the EU could rationalise and abolish refunds for certain products and destinations, he said, without giving examples.

Although the EU would maintain a restrictive export subsidy policy, it did not always mean cutting refunds, he said, adding export licence validity could be shortened or higher exporter deposits demanded.
